intro: A one-hot target puts all its mass on a single class. Label smoothing changes that target distribution, so even a confident correct prediction can still have a substantial loss.
task: Construct a softened target and calculate its cross-entropy from stable log probabilities. Track exactly where the smoothing mass goes.
requirements: logits is a nonempty (N,C) matrix with C>=2. targets is an integer vector of length N with labels in [0,C); boolean labels are invalid.
Require 0<=smoothing<=1. Assign 1-smoothing to the target class and smoothing/(C-1) to each other class.

Return the mean cross-entropy across examples as a scalar. Use stable log-softmax with no probability epsilon. This non-target-only convention differs from mixing a one-hot target with a uniform distribution over all C classes.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Check that each target sums to one
hints.body: There are C-1 non-target classes, not C, receiving the smoothing mass.

hints.title: Work from shifted logits
hints.body: Compute log probabilities directly so extreme incorrect predictions keep a finite, uncapped loss.

explanation: At smoothing zero the objective is ordinary multiclass cross-entropy. At smoothing one the originally correct class receives no mass; that boundary defines the formula rather than recommending a training choice.
The smoothing convention must be specified when comparing implementations. Assigning smoothing/C everywhere produces a different target and a different loss.
Ported the upstream non-target-only target distribution and stable log-softmax to NumPy. Added strict label/range validation and original fixtures.
